page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance, as measured by stress-ng, falls into the bottom 10%, indicating limited single-threaded execution speed. However, multi-core CPU performance scales to average levels, placing in the middle 50% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth exhibits a notable bottleneck: while small-block cached read operations perform at average speeds, large-block uncached read and write operations are weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

The hardware configuration supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES, and SHA_NI, which assist in cryptographic and compression tasks, as reflected in average scores for gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, the instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads that do not require high single-core performance or intensive uncached memory access. Typical workloads include static web serving, Redis database operations, and general-purpose application hosting.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 16 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor at 2.6 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 server lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct tradeoff: single-core CPU performance is poor, ranking in the bottom 10%, and uncached large-block memory bandwidth is weak. Conversely, multi-core CPU execution, cached memory reads, and cryptographic operations perform at average levels. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance suitable for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads, such as static web serving, Redis key-value stores, and standard database operations that do not demand high single-thread throughput.
